questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs show road rules you must follow.

questions.question: To help drivers merge from an entrance ramp into your lane, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Merge into the next lane, if possible.
Not worry about it, since they are the ones trying to merge.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Move to another lane if you can. This gives merging drivers plenty of space and helps prevent collisions.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the right side of your lane when hazards are on the left. Change your position as road conditions change.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel at a faster speed than usual to get to your destination more quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Decrease your following distance so you can be as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Stay flexible with your lane position at night. Use safe riding strategies in poor conditions.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid sudden moves.
Use both brakes.
Brake quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: If you are transporting a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean as you lean.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you during turns. They should sit forward without blocking your control and hold onto handholds or your waist.

questions.question: To be effective, a face shield should not:

options.text: Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.
Be airtight.
Fasten securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, give clear side vision, fit securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight shield causes fogging and blocks your view.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Use your high beam light, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use headlights ahead of you to see the road. Use your high beam, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not fully protect your eyes from wind. Wear goggles or a face shield for proper eye protection.

questions.question: When going through a turn on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused on the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead to where you want to go through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When braking normally, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Switch between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking alcohol, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with activities so they stop drinking.
Stop your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Let your friend ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your friend ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: There are several ways to stop someone from riding while impaired. You can arrange another way for them to get home, keep them busy with activities, use excuses to keep them from leaving before they are sober, and ask other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: What does a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects a rider's face during a crash.
Only protects riders from dirt.
Does not protect as well as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects a rider's face during a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What is the purpose of wearing the right clothing on a motorcycle?

options.text: It protects a rider in a crash.
It makes a rider look cool.
Style is more important than protection.
Clothes should be very loose-fitting.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects a rider in a crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing helps protect you in a crash. Wear sturdy, bright-colored, and reflective materials. Your clothes should fit snugly enough so they don't flap in the wind, but loosely enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How does braking in a turn compare to braking on a straight road?

options.text: It is easier than braking on a straight road.
It is harder than braking on a straight road.
It is safe to use only the front brake.
It is safe to use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes to brake in a turn, but you need proper technique and must be very careful.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT take to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Keep more distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near, and stay farther back from other vehicles. Watch vehicles ahead of you. Their headlights show the road ahead, and their taillights bounce when they go over bumps.

questions.question: The body removes about one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: To find how much alcohol remains, subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals about 4 drinks still in the body.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute.

questions.question: Riding alongside another rider:

options.text: Allows you to use more road space.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Allows you to talk to each other.
Makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle. It limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a quick stop, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers can see you easily.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about making sure others see you.
Ride aggressively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than cars, making them hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: A group of riders should pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, pass one rider at a time. Wait until the first rider returns safely to the original lane before the next rider passes. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.
